# `Ffi.Kernel`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Ffi.Kernel — the point-free primitive that aliases a stdlib member to a
compiler kernel.

Mental model: a kernel is a compiler-provided primitive (a Rust function in
the runtime) that no Ipê expression could implement — `String.length`,
`Time.now`, `Crypto.sha256`. `Ipe.Ffi.Kernel` is the one narrow doorway
through which an embedded-stdlib module names such a primitive:

```ipe
import Ipe.Ffi.Kernel as Kernel

length : String -> Int
length =
    Kernel.kernel "String_length"
```

The body is point-free by construction: `Kernel.kernel "<Name>"` IS the
member. The annotation above it is the whole contract — the compiler infers
nothing from the body — so the declared type is exactly the kernel's type,
checked against the kernel registry at compile time.

Trust boundary — this is a closed, compiler-only capability, not a user
escape hatch:

  * A `Kernel.kernel` call is accepted ONLY inside a driver-vouched embedded
    stdlib / FFI-interface module. The identical shape in ordinary user
    source is rejected fail-closed (IPE-N0042): user code can never mint a
    kernel, so it can never reach an unaudited runtime primitive by name.
  * The `"<Name>"` string is not free text: it must resolve to a registered
    kernel of the SAME type as the annotation, or the module fails to compile
    (IPE-N0028). There is no way to name a kernel that does not exist, and no
    way to give one the wrong type.

This module documents that surface for discoverability (`ipe doc`); it is a
compiler-internal qualifier, so importing it in your own code does not open a
kernel doorway — the origin gate above still applies.

## `kernel`

```ipe
kernel : String -> a
```

`kernel "<Name>"` — the member aliased to the registered compiler kernel
named `"<Name>"`.

The returned type is whatever the enclosing declaration's annotation says, so
the call is written point-free under a full signature:

```ipe
fromInt : Int -> String
fromInt =
    Kernel.kernel "String_fromInt"
```

`"<Name>"` is checked against the kernel registry: an unknown name, or a name
whose registered type disagrees with the annotation, is a compile error. The
call is legal only in a driver-vouched embedded-stdlib / FFI-interface module
(IPE-N0042 otherwise), so it is never an ambient capability of user code.
